items.title: 52193_Jay McShann oral history interview
items.q: Gene had been with her. But at this time, I got Gene, so that worked out good.

ctx.x: Oh, he was to stay with you quite a while.
Yes, Bob Mabane. Gene Ramey and -- let me see, the first drummer, and Pete McShann was the first drummer I had.

items.title: 68516_Gene Ramey oral history interview
items.q: We did that again with Jay McShann, too. ... Jay and I were brought to Chicago with a drummer who was supposed to have won, along there with George Barnes and Anita O'Day who also was supposed to have been the new stars for that time.

ctx.x: Well, how long would they walk?
Well, the contest would end when the last -- the next-to-last people fell out. And I don't remember just how long that was. We did that again with Jay McShann, too.
Well, they would walk, I take it, for a couple days, wouldn't they?

items.title: 68516_Gene Ramey oral history interview
items.q: those tunes that we brought over to McShann Max Hand's, some of them we had been playing with the Countess... And we were broadcasting every night.

ctx.x: : Bill Nolan -- he went with McShann too Chantue (phonetic), didn't he?
: Yeah, he came with McShann Max Hand's band later. And
: So, just let me get this again. Who was playing trumpet?

items.title: 68516_Gene Ramey oral history interview
items.q: I remember the situation with McShann Max Hana's band.

ctx.x: Well, what did you give as your reason for not --
Well, I just didn't want it, strictly because of the fact, first of all, because I remember the situation with McShann Max Hana's band.
